final_rationale: The verdict does not change. The Actor added no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the core missing predicates: no evidence of disclosure, no approved risk acceptance, no remediation, and no final legal resolution. That narrows the claim, but it is still only a reframing of the same record, not new support. The distinction matters: a caveated overall-readiness rationale might explain why certification was operationally attractive, but it does not satisfy the internal policy condition for compliance. Under the available evidence and policy text, the municipal permitting assistant gap remains a material limitation for a named launch use case, and the required disclosure-or-acceptance predicate remains unresolved. That leaves certification not evidentially supportable as compliant, even if the Actor now avoids overstating what the record proves.
remaining_concerns: The affected municipal permitting assistant segment is a named launch use case in two city pilot commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy standard.
The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The record still contains an open legal review ticket with no final answer on whether disclosure is required.
There is still no admissible evidence of pre-launch disclosure, approved risk acceptance, or remediation of the 1.3 percentage point gap before certification.
Aggregate readiness passing and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the separate disclosure predicate for a material named-use-case weakness.
